_meta.indication: Routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with hemophilia A or B with or without factor VIII or IX inhibitors.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, open-label study; 2:1 randomization to fitusiran 80 mg SC once monthly or BPA on demand
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and adolescent males aged ≥12 years with hemophilia A or B with inhibitors
pivotal_trials.endpoint: ABR (annualized bleeding rate) in the efficacy period
pivotal_trials.result: 91% reduction in ABR for treated bleeds vs BPA on-demand (p<0.0001)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, open-label study; 2:1 randomization to fitusiran 80 mg SC once monthly or CFCs on demand
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and adolescent males aged ≥12 years with hemophilia A or B without inhibitors
pivotal_trials.endpoint: ABR (annualized bleeding rate) in the efficacy period
pivotal_trials.result: 90% reduction in ABR for treated bleeds vs factor on-demand (p<0.0001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%): viral infection (29%), nasopharyngitis (26%), and bacterial infection (11%). Serious risks include thromboembolic events and gallbladder disease (boxed warning) and hepatotoxicity.
target_moa: A double-stranded siRNA that degrades antithrombin (AT) mRNA via RNA interference on the SERPINC1 gene, reducing plasma AT levels; AT normally inactivates thrombin (factor IIa) and factor Xa, so lowering it rebalances hemostasis.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: THROMBOTIC EVENTS AND ACUTE AND RECURRENT GALLBLADDER DISEASE — serious thrombotic events (risk factors include persistent AT activity <15%, 80 mg once monthly dosing, indwelling venous catheters, post-operative setting) and acute/recurrent gallbladder disease, some requiring cholecystectomy or with complications such as pancreatitis.

companion_dx_detail: INNOVANCE Antithrombin assay, FDA-authorized as a companion diagnostic to measure AT activity and adjust fitusiran dosing to target AT activity of 15-35%.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; the application did not raise efficacy or safety issues requiring external expert advice.

basis.text: Granted breakthrough therapy designation on December 6, 2023, for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in patients with hemophilia B with factor IX inhibitors.

orphan_indication.text: Granted orphan drug designation on August 16, 2013 for treatment of hemophilia A and August 12, 2013 for treatment of hemophilia B.

citations.quote: Fitusiran was granted orphan drug designation (ODD) on August 16, 2013, for the treatment of hemophilia A (ODD #13-4028) and August 12, 2013, for the treatment of hemophilia B (ODD #13-4029).

basis.text: The application was a standard review.

summary.text: QFITLIA (fitusiran) was approved under standard review, supported by two adequate and well-controlled trials (EFC14768 and EFC14769); it had orphan drug, fast track, and breakthrough therapy designations, and its approval was accompanied by FDA authorization of the INNOVANCE Antithrombin companion diagnostic.
